headline_marked: AL leader [[Mahbub ul Alam Hanif sentenced to death]] for crimes against humanity
headline: AL leader Mahbub ul Alam Hanif sentenced to death for crimes against humanity
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has sentenced the banned Awami League's joint general secretary to death and three others to life imprisonment for their roles in the July uprising.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has sentenced Mahbub ul Alam Hanif, joint general secretary of the banned Awami League, to death for crimes against humanity committed during the July mass uprising.
Three other defendants—Sadar Uddin Khan, Asgar Ali, and Ataur Rahman—were sentenced to life imprisonment with hard labor.
The tribunal also ordered that half of the immovable property of the four convicted leaders be confiscated to compensate victims and their families through the July Foundation.
The court found Hanif guilty of inciting and ordering cadres and security forces to fire on protesters in Kushtia on August 5, 2024, resulting in six deaths.
The victims were identified as Ashraful Islam, Suruj Ali, Abdullah Al Mustakin, Mo. Usama, Babul Farazi, and Yusuf Sheikh.
Hanif was also convicted of overseeing torture, illegal detention, and denying medical care to hundreds of unarmed civilians and students in Kushtia and other regions.
The tribunal ruled that the defendants conspired with the ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's cabinet to lethally suppress the 'March to Dhaka' program.
All four convicted individuals, including Hanif, are currently fugitives.
This marks the eighth verdict in cases related to the July uprising, with 72 people sentenced so far, including 23 death sentences.
caption:
Death sentence for AL leader Mahbub ul Alam Hanif. He was convicted of ordering the killing of 6 protesters in Kushtia.

The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has sentenced Mahbub ul Alam Hanif, joint general secretary of the banned Awami League, to death for crimes against humanity committed during the July mass uprising.

Three other defendants—Sadar Uddin Khan, Asgar Ali, and Ataur Rahman—were sentenced to life imprisonment with hard labor.

The tribunal also ordered that half of the immovable property of the four convicted leaders be confiscated to compensate victims and their families through the July Foundation.

The court found Hanif guilty of inciting and ordering cadres and security forces to fire on protesters in Kushtia on August 5, 2024, resulting in six deaths.

The victims were identified as Ashraful Islam, Suruj Ali, Abdullah Al Mustakin, Mo. Usama, Babul Farazi, and Yusuf Sheikh.

Hanif was also convicted of overseeing torture, illegal detention, and denying medical care to hundreds of unarmed civilians and students in Kushtia and other regions.

The tribunal ruled that the defendants conspired with the ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's cabinet to lethally suppress the 'March to Dhaka' program.

All four convicted individuals, including Hanif, are currently fugitives.

This marks the eighth verdict in cases related to the July uprising, with 72 people sentenced so far, including 23 death sentences.

headline: 3,430 workers to be hired by Dhaka's two city corporations
summary: The Local Government Ministry has approved the recruitment of daily-wage workers for waste removal, cleaning, and mosquito control.
details: The Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) and Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) will recruit approximately 3,430 workers on a daily-wage basis. DSCC will hire 2,026 workers, while DNCC will recruit 1,404.
caption:
Dhaka's city corporations are hiring over 3,000 workers to clean the capital. But will the process be transparent?

The Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) and Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) will recruit approximately 3,430 workers on a daily-wage basis. DSCC will hire 2,026 workers, while DNCC will recruit 1,404.
